name: catacomb3d
title: Catacomb 3-D: The Descent (id Software / Softdisk, Borland C++ / DOS)
_doc: THE SECOND 16-BIT TARGET, built with Keen Dreams' recipe: the same id engine generation (ID_CA, ID_MM, ID_VW, ID_US, ID_SD, ID_IN), the same Borland C++ 2.0, the same MODEL MEDIUM. What it adds is a first-person view drawn by code the program writes at run time: C3_SCALE.C compiles a scaler per wall height (BuildCompScale: `mov al,[si+n]` / `and es:[di+ofs],al` / `retf`) and a drawing routine per shape (BuildCompShape), which ScaleWalls (C3_ASM.ASM) and ScaleShape's inline assembly enter with a far call.
_units: The project's own item list, read out of CAT3D.PRJ in order. 17 units.
_compile: The options PRJCFG reads out of CAT3D.PRJ (goldens/borland-prj.json, gate-borland-options): -mm -a and, unlike Keen Dreams, no -K, so plain char is SIGNED; enums are int by BCC's default.
_tasm: The four Turbo Assembler modules CAT3D.PRJ builds (ID_VW_A.ASM includes ID_VW_AE.ASM), held to TASM 2.5 by gate-tasm-front. ID_US_A.ASM keeps its random-number table in FARDATA. JABHACK.ASM is `.386C`: CheckIs386 tests FLAGS bits 12-15 and, on a 386, jabhack2 patches Borland's long-division helper LDIV@ to an INT 60h handler that divides with IDIV on 32 bits. This machine is a 286 -- PUSHF keeps those bits clear -- so the program's own test answers no and the 386 path is never taken; its instructions are translated to refusals that name themselves if they ever run.
_dataObjects: The six data objects CAT3D.PRJ links, read as they stand in the tree (src/asm/omf.js): each is one segment holding one public at offset 0 and no fixups -- the dictionaries in DGROUP, the headers and the intro screen in far segments of their own. They describe the game data they were built with; the data itself is not in the tree.
